label: Data clean enough to normalize (75-80%)
kill_criterion: Normalization error rate on real mixed-vendor data exceeds the threshold where a QBR number can be defended, producing wrong figures in client-facing output.
test_that_resolves_it: Run normalization on 3 anonymized real mixed-vendor datasets; measure field-level error/conflict rate against ground truth.
evidence: [A] CS:LOW - Vision Risk Register ~30%, P0, UNOWNED, no study run.

label: The 15-minute edit fits
kill_criterion: Operators take substantially longer than 15 min to edit-and-trust the draft, or discard it and write from scratch.
test_that_resolves_it: Timed operator prototype session: draft handed to a real vCIO/account manager, measure time-to-send and whether they trust the numbers.
evidence: [A] CS:LOW - ~35%, P0, UNOWNED, no study run.

label: WTP holds vs buy-vs-build
kill_criterion: Target MSPs decline to pay ACP's price because they self-build (small/technical) or already have it (large).
test_that_resolves_it: Van Westendorp / Gabor-Granger pricing test with the 20-100 client, 10-50 tech segment.
evidence: [A] CS:MEDIUM - flat per-tech anchors only; Derek self-builds, Vikram already-has.

label: ScalePad displacement window open
kill_criterion: ScalePad Lifecycle Manager X is not actually being discontinued, or the window closes before ACP ships.
test_that_resolves_it: Confirm ScalePad roadmap via second source; track migration timing.

label: Review/edit-before-send is wanted
kill_criterion: MSPs want fully-autonomous send (no edit), or reject AI authorship entirely - either invalidates the edit-before-send mechanic.
test_that_resolves_it: Confirmed; monitor in operator session for whether edit is cosmetic or substantive.

label: QBR demand exists (the destination)
kill_criterion: QBR demand collapses under independent quant (Qualtrics n=500) or proves an artifact of the shared 8-person qual base.
evidence: [D] CS:HIGH - #1 across 3 instruments; two share the same 8 people, only n=39 adds independent n.

label: First-party full-stack telemetry is a real, defensible moat
kill_criterion: Competitors normalize adequately via third-party APIs, or the moat only covers N-able's own stack (not cross-vendor), collapsing the differentiation.
test_that_resolves_it: Scope which vendors' data is legally accessible (see H2); measure normalization quality first-party vs third-party API.
evidence: [A] CS:MEDIUM - moat asserted but unbuilt (normalization Not started).

label: Demand is for THIS solution, not just the destination
kill_criterion: Operators want the cross-stack QBR outcome but reject the 'AI drafts, you edit and defend' mechanism - they want the number handed over, not a draft to babysit.
test_that_resolves_it: Solution-fit operator session: present the draft-then-edit mechanic, observe whether it matches how they actually want the job done.
evidence: [A] CS:MEDIUM - all demand data measured desire for the outcome, never for this mechanism.

label: No account-ending wrong-number event in front of a client
kill_criterion: A normalized figure is wrong in a client boardroom, the client catches it, and the MSP loses trust in A permanently (asymmetric, unrecoverable).
test_that_resolves_it: Add defensibility tiering (Measured/Benchmarked/Estimated/Unverified) to the QBR NARRATIVE, not just the ledger; test error-surfacing UX.
evidence: [A] - asymmetric high-consequence risk, unmodeled; narrative layer has no defensibility tiering.

label: Cross-vendor data egress is legally and contractually permitted
kill_criterion: Competing vendors' ToS/DPA prohibit N-able extracting and normalizing their data into a client-facing artifact, OR client consent for cross-tenant data use is not obtainable - collapsing cross-vendor to cross-N-able-stack.
test_that_resolves_it: Legal/DPA review + read one competitor vendor ToS (ThreatLocker/Rapid7); confirm client-consent path in multi-tenant.
evidence: [?] - unexamined; the moat 'normalize from inside' only holds for N-able's own stack. Possibly fatal to the cross-vendor promise.

label: The operator (not just the buyer) adopts
kill_criterion: The vCIO/account manager/senior tech who runs the QBR routes around A or rejects it; tool becomes owner-bought shelfware.
test_that_resolves_it: Operator ethnography + prototype session (collapses with A10 and A2 into one study).
evidence: [A] CS:HIGH - ~93% [A]; every demand number is buyer purchase-intent, operator never studied (vision-synthesis section 5).

label: Quarterly cadence survives a monthly subscription model
kill_criterion: A tool used 4x/year cannot form a habit; MSPs feel monthly cost against quarterly value and churn; cold-start each quarter degrades experience.
test_that_resolves_it: Model retention curve for a 4x/year tool on a monthly plan; consider bundling A with a daily-use coworker (Triage) for cadence support.
evidence: [A] - cadence/pricing mismatch, unmodeled. Contrast daily-compounding Ticket Triage.

label: MSP brand is not homogenized by an AI house style
kill_criterion: QBRs from different MSPs read identically ('the ACP look'), eroding the client-facing differentiation MSPs pay for; or an AI tell damages the MSP's brand.
test_that_resolves_it: Blind read: can a client tell two different MSPs' ACP-generated QBRs apart? Test voice-customization depth.
evidence: [A] - unexamined; directly contradicts 'the MSP owns the voice' claim.

label: The edit paradox is resolvable (fast AND defensible)
kill_criterion: Trust-enough-to-be-fast and understand-enough-to-defend are mutually exclusive; the operator must pick one, breaking either the 15-min claim or the 'defend every number' claim.
test_that_resolves_it: Operator session measuring BOTH time-to-send AND ability to correctly answer a challenge to a specific number.
evidence: [A] - structural tension between the speed value prop and the defensibility value prop.

label: A does not cannibalize N-able's own reporting products
kill_criterion: A displaces existing UEM/Cove/Adlumin reporting revenue and triggers internal margin/channel conflict; strategy-fit cannot be confirmed.
test_that_resolves_it: Cannot fully test until FY27 strategy loads; scope overlap with existing reporting SKUs internally.
evidence: [?] - n-able-strategy-context.md is a v0 placeholder; internal cannibalization cost unmodeled.

label: LLM cost per QBR fits inside the flat-WTP margin
kill_criterion: Large-context cross-stack generation x (clients x 4 quarters x edit loops) produces COGS that inverts gross margin at the $25-50/tech/mo ceiling.
test_that_resolves_it: Model token cost of one full cross-stack QBR generation + edit loop; multiply by realistic client/quarter volume; compare to WTP ceiling.
evidence: [?] - unit economics unmodeled; DSE helps runbooks not free-form narrative.

label: Output is not pulled into an insurer/auditor reliance chain
kill_criterion: A client's cyber-insurer or auditor relies on an ACP-QBR number that is wrong, creating multi-party reliance-chain liability.
test_that_resolves_it: Legal scoping: is QBR output 'advisory' or 'relied-upon'? Define disclaimer + defensibility-tier requirements.
evidence: [?] - legal scope undefined; QBR content may enter the same reliance chain flagged for IR/RCA (#1 on cyber-insurance policies).

label: Multi-tenant approval authority is resolvable
kill_criterion: Approval authority must cascade to the end-customer admin in multi-tenant, breaking A's frictionless-draft promise at the tenancy boundary.
test_that_resolves_it: Resolve build approval-model open questions OQ-001..005; test multi-tenant data-use approval flow.
evidence: [?] - build has 5 open approval-model questions (OQ-001..005, findings JSON).
